title: A dense quasi-compact refinement is cartesian over the distinguished open
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, and let $c,d$ be compactifications of $f$ [def-nagata-compactification]. Let $r:c.Z\to d.Z$ satisfy $c.i;r=d.i$ and $r;d.g=c.g$, the two upstream refinement triangles [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Assume that $c.i$ is quasi-compact and scheme-theoretically dominant [def-nagata-dense-compactification]. Then the square with top map $c.i$, left map $\mathrm{id}_X$, right map $r$, and bottom map $d.i$ is cartesian [def-pc-base-change]. No quasi-compactness or density of $d.i$ is required.

proof.text: Let P be the fibre product of r.hom with d.i, and let t:X → P be the lift of c.i and the identity of X. The two projections satisfy t ≫ fst = c.i and t ≫ snd = id. The ambient map r.hom is proper by proper-over-separated [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated], so snd is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Its section t is therefore a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]. These are the first half of the existing Lean proof, not new unproved obligations.

The projection fst is an open immersion, hence a flat monomorphism. The square expressing t as the base change of t ≫ fst along fst is cartesian because fst is mono. Flat base change of scheme-theoretic dominance gives dominance of t from that of c.i, with quasi-compactness supplied by the hypothesis on c.i. This is precisely the proved source lemma IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.of_comp used in RefinementPullback. Thus t has zero kernel. A closed immersion with zero kernel is an isomorphism (IsClosedImmersion.isIso_iff_ker_eq_bot).

The canonical comparison t from X to P is now an isomorphism respecting both projections. IsPullback.of_iso_pullback therefore proves that the square with sides c.i, id_X, r.hom and d.i is cartesian. This is exactly the existing theorem, whose built-in axiom guard excludes sorryAx.
